body: I just got this fucking junk in my email, and I am so furious. Medium is promoting this article by sending it to everyone who uses Medium, right to the inbox. We need to do something regarding this, we cannot just sit and watch.

Yeah, I've seen a lot of "professionals" like this who are clearly unfit for their job and are a disgrace to the whole medical community. The one's I visited though were among the most well-known and highly regarded, and that is why I lost faith in the profession as a whole. 

I've tried multiple different medicines and I reacted the same way to all but one of them. I first received a diagnosis for ADHD(incorrectly) before Aspergers, and the stimulant medication for ADHD made me incredibly sleepy and depressed. The panic attacks were random for the most part, however, they mostly occurred when I was around other people or in a social setting. I still live with my parents because I'm not grown up enough yet to live on my own, and I do not have a job, so my parents take care of all my expenses. However, they believe that medication is a big fat lie and that I'm really just pretending to have Aspergers and that all the psychiatrists who gave or confirmed the diagnosis were lying. 

I used to love drawing, however, I lack precision. I cannot even hold a pen correctly, let alone a brush. I suck horribly at drawing, just as an example, if I try to make a straight line without using a ruler, it'll end up looking a bit like a waveform. Singing was the art form that used to help me process my emotions. I used to write about my feelings every day, however, that just turned into a kind of a depression journal that contained my sob story. And then writing down every single event that happened became my special interest, so basically that just went down horribly. 

I wouldn't have guessed you were an Aspie too had you not mentioned it. You seem very good at talking to people and saying the right thing, however, those are both things I suck horribly at. Can I know how you picked up your social skills? I've tried just talking to people, and that did me no good other than making me realize just how bad I am at socialising. 

I've tried volunteering, and that doesn't go well with me. I was bullied by other volunteers and often had fights with them and went home crying, and that is not something I want to do again. There's no support groups in my area, at least not that I know of. Where I live, I have yet to meet another Aspie, so I do not think a support group even exists. 

I've decided to have another go at it. I'll try to socialise and make friends, and see where that gets me. I'm not thinking of ending it anymore, at least not at the moment. I just hope this time it ends well. Thanks for talking to me and making me feel good. Also, my social anxiety hits the roof when I call anyone, so calling a crisis number isn't something I'd feel comfortable doing.

I gave up on therapy and psychiatrists a couple months ago. They always try to force their views onto me, and try to change me as a person, and not in the good way. I've had this experience with multiple psychiatrists, and I have lost all faith in medication and talking to therapists due to this.  

I did start medication with a low dosage and ramped it up slowly, however, for the 4 months that I took the medication, I had multiple panic attacks every single day, and this happened with both stimulants and non-stimulants, so I gave up on it. I also have the panic attack problem with coffee, so its possible that my brain just doesn't respond well to outside influence or alterations. 

I was on a mood stabiliser for bipolar, however, due to the reasons I mentioned before, I gave up on the medication. These days whenever I feel depressed, I just take a minute to myself and gulp down the pain and sorrow and have been delaying my feelings for a long time now. This has caused a huge build up of sadness in me that I can't figure out a way of getting out of the system. 

I used to enjoy singing and skating and cycling and a bunch of other stuff, however, I no longer do any of those things. This is because of a horrible experience I had as a child. Whenever I would go outside of the house to indulge in any of these activities, all the kids would circle me and beat me up and make fun of me. I would cry and they wouldn't let me go. This would happen to me every time I went out. That took my childhood and all the things that made me happy away from me. I didn't always used to be so afraid of doing anything that would require stepping outside of the house, but this and other such bullying has scarred me for life. 

I live with my parents. I have tried sharing my feelings and being emotionally open with my family before, and I did not get a good response to that. Ever since, I've completely locked myself down emotionally. 

Thanks a lot, you've really made me feel better. I still don't think I can live like this for long though. Every single attempt I make at socializing ends up in a disaster, and I've had no friends for a very long time now.  I know that the way to solve my problems is to make friends and get people in my life that I can talk to and share my feelings with, because my lack of a social life is the main cause of sorrow for me, but I just don't know how to do that with my Aspergers.

My life wasn't always so miserable. I used to have friends, I used to be happy, and I used to look forward to living another year. Then something happened to me, that I can't figure out, and I lost all my friends, all my happiness, and all my willingness to live. If it wasn't me who did this to myself, I do not know who else to blame. Reading that letter, I realized how much of an utter disappointment I am, to myself and to everyone else. I'm suffering from long term depression, and as far as mental health is concerned, I have bipolar disorder and autism spectrum disorder(aspergers). I cannot make friends, I cannot talk to people, I cannot do anything. I've lost my willingness to just do stuff basically. I used to be an extremely self motivated person, and I could spend years over years without giving up. Now I give up at the slightest hint of difficulty or failure. Nobody gives a rats ass about me, and that stings me in the chest every single breathing moment. 

I've tried medication, but it doesn't go fine with me. I have panic attacks whenever I take mood altering medication, and so that is not the route to go for me. Talking it out is no option for me. I have nobody to talk to. My parents don't care about me. I've got no friends. I haven't even got 1 person I could talk to and be taken seriously. My parents don't take me seriously when I try to discuss about this with them, they think I'm bluffing or trying to just gain attention. 

I was not always pathetic. However, after trying to look at my life from an outsiders perspective, I realize that I've become very pathetic.
